domains.title: Warrior City
domains.subtitle: The domain of Spártē
domains.lead: In the greek location tradition, Spártē governed warrior city. The name encodes a sphere of power that shaped ritual, narrative, and social order.

cards.title: Primary Sphere
cards.body: Spártē is principally associated with warrior city.

cards.title: Cultural Role
cards.body: Worshippers approached Spártē through cult, myth, and the material culture of the greek-location world.

mythology.lead: The myths of Spártē preserve the name's power and personality across generations of retelling.

myths.title: The story of Spártē
myths.text: Spártē appears in greek location tradition as a figure whose domain over warrior city shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Spártē's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Spártē in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Spártē carries within it a greek location understanding of sown land (from σπείρω). Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
